requirement:
The harness instructs the model to finish by calling
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission` has one clause: "The harness instructs the model to finish by calling" the tool described in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`. That clause describes observable behavior: the model is told to finish by calling the submission tool. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface.

I considered the clause as a possible structural obligation. An alternative could put the instruction in the system prompt, the first user message or a tool description. Another could build the instruction text from a template or a literal string. Each alternative gives the model the same instruction, so how the instruction is delivered is discretionary.

The tool shape is `submit_result({result: R})`, with a schema derived from `R: JsonSchema` by `schemars`. That belongs to the separate requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`. This requirement only cites it for context. Any structural obligations there are assessed against that requirement's own text.

There are no implementation roots and no acknowledgments, and none are needed. No structural obligation here requires implementation evidence.

behavioral: The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission` has one behavioral obligation. The harness must instruct the model to finish by calling `submit_result`. The tool's schema and argument shape belong to `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`, which the subject only cites. I did not request implementation source.

The reviewed tests check that instruction in each place the harness builds a request:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` serializes the first request's `chat_history` for the generic `ToolAgent` path. It asserts that the history contains "Finish by calling submit_result". The same test checks that the reminder after a text-only reply says to invoke `submit_result` exactly once.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` checks every one of the four requests sent to a local OpenAI-style transport. Each request's serialized `input` must contain "Finish by calling submit_result". The test also checks that `submit_result` is among the offered tools.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_ollama_backend_delivers_tools_and_results_over_native_chat]` checks both native Ollama chat requests. Each request's `messages` must contain "Finish by calling submit_result".

The assertions are specific to the instruction text, and each test is marked `{test}` for the subject. I found no input class or scenario that would let the harness omit the instruction while these tests still passed.

The tool schema and the effect of an accepted call are delegated to `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. They are not assessed here.
